Complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger in Chai Prakan, and approval of a study visit on carbon credits in Trat
se: The committee considered a complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger in Chai Prakan district, Chiang Mai, and invited the agencies concerned to give information. The Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation said the area in question lies outside the planned Doi Wiang Pha National Park, which covers about 189,151 rai after its boundary was revised in September 2025. The Royal Forest Department said part of the area is in the Mae Fang watershed national reserved forest. Residents who pass screening under the Cabinet resolution of 26 November 2018 receive a certificate of rights that forbids selling, renting or transferring the land; if it is found to be rented out, the rights are withdrawn and the land is taken back. In this area the survey is still at the screening stage and no rights have been granted. The Department of Provincial Administration said sub-district heads, village heads and sub-district administrative organisation chiefs have a duty to prevent and watch for forest encroachment. The Office of the National Land Policy Board explained the conditions for community land allocation: the land must be used by the holder, cannot change hands, but can be inherited. Chiang Mai province said the district held a meeting of its forest protection subcommittee and ordered a survey: land encroached before 2014 will remain with residents, while land encroached after 2014 will all be taken back and restored as forest. The Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division said that since May 2026 it has taken part in 5 cases of forest encroachment for ginger in the area. The meeting approved a study visit on carbon credits in Trat on 11–13 December 2026 and set the next meeting for Tuesday 24 November 2026. The complaint is an allegation that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger, Chai Prakan district, Chiang Mai (Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, Royal Forest Department, Department of Provincial Administration, Office of the National Land Policy Board, Chiang Mai province, Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division)

How to prosecute illegal dumping of industrial and hazardous waste
se: The committee studied how to prosecute those who illegally dump industrial and hazardous waste on private land in Phachi district, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya; Ban Khai district, Rayong; Si Thep district, Phetchabun; Klang Dong district, Nakhon Ratchasima; and Rang Bua subdistrict, Chom Bueng district, Ratchaburi, with the Lawyers Council of Thailand under the Royal Patronage invited. Representatives of the public described the hardship caused by factories and chemical warehouses in the areas, which affect the environment and health and have caught fire several times; this is information from complainants that the agencies are still checking.
it: How to prosecute illegal dumping of industrial and hazardous waste (Lawyers Council)
